what: The op prompt states as a MUST that INPUT_TAGGERS declare tag_gamma_dtype / tag_gamma_layout returning the "none" sentinel. Following that instruction would BREAK the golden suite: cartesian() removes every tagger key from the iterated finite axes ("the tagger wins - the axis is not iterated"), and gamma dtype/layout are not derivable from the input SHAPE tuple a tagger receives, so declaring them collapses both axes to one value and silently deletes ~2/3 of the gamma cartesian. The correct wiring (what the op does) is to leave them as finite TARGET axes and read them off the tensor inside validate(); the prompt reads as if that were non-compliant. A future agent asked to enforce prompt MUSTs could "fix" this and gut the suite with no failing test.
suggest: Reword that prompt section: gamma_dtype/gamma_layout are FINITE iterated axes, not shape-derived - validate() (and axes.py classify_call) must map absent gamma to "none", and they must NOT be declared in INPUT_TAGGERS. Add the general rule to REGISTRY_MODEL.md: only declare a tagger for an axis whose value is computable from the inputs tuple, because a tagger key overrides the TARGET iteration.

what: The verifier CLI prints NOTHING to stdout and exits 1, while still writing a complete --output JSON. Reproduced three times (piped, redirected to a file, and with python3 -u): the only stdout is the ttnn import banner. My prompt says "The CLI emits a categorized report. Read every loud category" - it does not emit one, so I had to hand-load a 25 MB verifier_report.json and aggregate summary/by_category myself, and the nonzero exit initially read as a crash on a run that was in fact perfectly clean (supported_fail=xpass_drift=xfail_wrong_mode=0).
suggest: Have the CLI print the summary table (the seven category counts + the loud-category node ids) to stdout, and exit 0 when all three loud categories are zero (reserve nonzero for a real drift/failure signal). Until then, the verifier prompt should say the report is JSON-only and show the two-line json.load snippet.

ref: verifier prompt Testing Protocol step 2 + eval/eval_test_runner.sh
what: A full golden run for this op takes ~20 min wall (5 min JIT precompile warm pass + ~7 min graded run + device reset) but the Bash tool caps at a 10-minute timeout, so the straightforward foreground invocation the prompt prescribes is SIGTERMed mid-run - losing the run, leaving /tmp/tt-device.dirty set, and producing a results dir that looks populated but is stale. The prompt forbids background execution only for run_safe_pytest.sh and tt-probe.sh, so whether eval_test_runner.sh may be backgrounded is undefined; the working pattern (nohup + poll runner.log for the "N/M passed" line) is documented nowhere.
suggest: In the verifier prompt, state that the golden run routinely exceeds the tool timeout, that eval_test_runner.sh (unlike run_safe_pytest.sh) IS safe to nohup because it holds the device flock itself, and give the poll idiom. Also have the runner write a status/DONE sentinel file so a poller does not have to grep the log text.

ref: verifier prompt, Perf refinements: "an attention: note on the entry"
what: The prompt tells the verifier to find the mandatory perf target by an `attention:` comment on a LOOSE_CASES entry. eval/golden_tests/rms_norm/feature_spec.py carries no such marker - the perf corpus is instead marked with group="perf" plus extras (achievable_ns, measured_on, reference_aiclk_mhz, minimum_expected_speedup) and a prose comment ("A marginal win is not sufficient here... expected to expose a decisively better architecture") on one case. The two vocabularies do not meet, so identifying THE flagged shape is a judgement call rather than a lookup, and a future verifier could conclude no case is flagged and free-select its own region.
suggest: Align the two: either have /golden-tests emit the attention: note, or teach the verifier prompt the real convention - group=="perf" marks the mandatory targets, and extras.minimum_expected_speedup (when present) marks the decisive one whose goal is scaled_reference_ns / minimum_expected_speedup.
